title: Fluffy Mashed Potato Dinner Rolls
changes_from_base: Riced potato and its cooking water replace the milk paste; rolls baked separately on a tray.
summary: Featherlight dinner rolls made with mashed potato and its cooking water, baked individually for a golden crust all round.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel
baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or russet), peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.note: beaten with 1 tsp water and a pinch of salt

steps.title: Potato
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold unsalted water, bring to the boil and simmer 8-10 min, until tender. Scoop out 75 ml of the cooking water to cool, drain, then return the potatoes to the hot pan for a minute to steam dry.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Rice or mash until completely smooth, weigh out 225 g (any extra is cook's perks) and stir in the butter until it melts.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl, add the warm potato and rub together with your fingers. Add 1 egg and the cooled potato water and knead 8-10 min by machine on low, until soft, smooth and a little sticky.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover and leave 30-40 min, until nearly doubled; the potato makes it rise quickly.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Pat the dough into a 20 cm square and cut it into 12 equal pieces. Round each into a ball and space them 5 cm apart on the tray. Cover loosely and leave 30-40 min, until puffy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Brush with the egg wash and bake 15-18 min, until golden brown; the centre of a roll reads 88-90 °C. Cool on a rack at least 10 min.

tips: Steam the potatoes dry in the pan so the dough does not turn gluey.
The potato starch keeps the rolls soft for an extra day.
Leave the potato water unsalted; the salt is measured in the dough.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
